title: В холодильной камере  (In the Walk-In Fridge)

segments.t: Chaos erupts in two places at once: at the police station, Roma's mother spots her little boy with Max, while back at the restaurant Senya and Fedya trap German inside the walk-in fridge.
Мы попытались, у нас не получилось.
Let's go through each line of the double predicament.
'Here is this little boy!' Adding the emphatic particle right after 'here is' expresses sudden recognition.
'Wait, I will explain everything right now.' Here Max anchors the thought on 'wait' and finishes on 'will explain', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
'Come on in, dear guests.' Putting the adjective 'dear' after the noun 'guests' gives a traditional, ironic Russian welcome.
Мы попытались, у нас не получилось.
'We tried, it did not work out for us.' Success or failure in Russian is expressed impersonally: literally 'by us it did not turn out'.
'A dubious way to stop me.' Notice how Russian puts 'dubious' and 'to stop' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
'That is it, I am leaving.' In spoken Russian, saying 'I went' in the past tense means 'I'm off' or 'I'm leaving right now'.
'Close the walk-in fridge quickly!' In a restaurant kitchen, the walk-in cooler is simply called 'the chamber'.
'Let's not shout.' Starting with the everyday word for 'let us' is how Russian speakers warmly invite someone to do something together.
'Calm down, everyone, please.' Max uses a polite everyday Russian courtesy expression that sets the tone of the conversation right away.
'This is Konstantin Anisimov's child.' Max centers this short reply on 'child', letting a few direct words carry the whole meaning.
'Do you know Konstantin?' In spoken Russian, the words stay in their normal statement order and Max's rising voice at the end turns the line into a question.
'Then where is our child?' The adverb 'then' links the realization to the urgent question 'where'. Now let's hear the whole scene again at natural speed.
Мы попытались, у нас не получилось.
Notice the very common Russian idiom 'it did not work out for us', which uses the neuter past reflexive verb with 'by us'. Until next time!

lines.fragment: мы попытались, попытались, у нас не получилось
